interactions.label: A 48-year-old man with uncontrolled T2DM (HbA1c 9.2%) visits your NCD clinic. Us

params.question: A 48-year-old man with uncontrolled T2DM (HbA1c 9.2%) visits your NCD clinic. Using the 5As dietary counselling framework, what should you do FIRST?

answers.text: Advise him to replace polished rice with millets and increase dietary fibre

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Advise is the third step of the 5As. Without first understanding the patient's current dietary habits (Ask) and identifying key risk areas (Assess), your advice may miss the most impactful changes for this individual.

answers.text: Assess his BMI, waist circumference, and HbA1c

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Assess follows Ask in the 5As sequence. You need the patient's own account of their diet before interpreting anthropometric and biochemical data in a dietary context.

answers.text: Ask him to describe his dietary intake using a 24-hour recall

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Ask is the first step — a simple 24-hour recall ('What did you eat from waking to sleeping yesterday?') opens the dietary history and lets you tailor all subsequent steps to this patient's actual habits.

answers.text: Assist him by preparing a written meal plan with calorie targets

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Assist is the fourth step. A personalised meal plan is most effective after you have identified the patient's specific high-impact dietary changes through Ask, Assess, and Advise.

overallFeedback.feedback: The 5As framework follows a fixed sequence: Ask → Assess → Advise → Assist → Arrange. Always begin by asking about the patient's current dietary intake through a simple 24-hour recall.

Correct! The 5As framework always begins with Ask — screening for dietary risk through a 24-hour recall and targeted questions about fried food, sugar, and processed snacks before moving to assessment and advice.

interactions.label: Most breastfeeding problems such as nipple pain, engorgement, and mastitis are c

params.question: Most breastfeeding problems such as nipple pain, engorgement, and mastitis are caused by insufficient milk production.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Most breastfeeding problems — nipple pain, engorgement, mastitis, and even perceived insufficient milk — trace back to incorrect positioning or poor latch as their root cause. Correcting the latch is the highest-yield clinical intervention.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Incorrect positioning or poor latch — not insufficient milk production — is the root cause of most breastfeeding problems. Correcting the latch is the single highest-yield intervention in any breastfeeding support encounter.

params.question: The WHO defines Minimum Acceptable Diet (MAD) for children aged 6–23 months as meeting which combination of criteria?

answers.text: Minimum dietary diversity (≥3 of 8 food groups) AND minimum meal frequency

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Three food groups is too low. The WHO threshold for minimum dietary diversity is ≥5 of 8 food groups, ensuring the child receives adequate macro- and micronutrient variety.

answers.text: Minimum dietary diversity (≥5 of 8 food groups) AND minimum meal frequency

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: MAD requires BOTH minimum dietary diversity (≥5 of 8 food groups) AND minimum meal frequency. NFHS-5 found only 20.7% of Indian children aged 6–23 months meet this combined standard.

answers.text: Minimum dietary diversity (≥5 of 8 food groups) AND minimum energy intake in kilocalories

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While energy intake matters clinically, the WHO MAD indicator pairs dietary diversity with meal frequency — not absolute kilocalorie intake. Meal frequency serves as a practical proxy for adequate energy.

answers.text: Minimum dietary diversity (≥4 food groups) AND consumption of iron-rich foods

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Four food groups was the older minimum dietary diversity threshold. The current WHO IYCF framework uses ≥5 of 8 food groups; iron-rich food consumption is tracked as a separate IYCF indicator, not part of MAD.

overallFeedback.feedback: MAD is defined as meeting BOTH minimum dietary diversity (≥5 of 8 food groups) AND minimum meal frequency. NFHS-5 found that only 20.7% of Indian children aged 6–23 months achieve this combined standard — one of the lowest rates in the region.

Correct! MAD combines dietary diversity (≥5 of 8 food groups) with meal frequency — yet only 20.7% of Indian children aged 6–23 months meet this standard, meaning roughly 75 million children receive suboptimal complementary feeding.

params.question: You are planning a community nutrition education session on complementary feeding at an urban health centre. What is the recommended approach for the opening segment?

answers.text: Present WHO IYCF guidelines using a projected slideshow

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Starting with a didactic presentation misses the opportunity to understand participants' current practices and build engagement. The opening should be participatory, not lecture-based.

answers.text: Ask participants what they currently feed their infants to establish baseline and build engagement

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Asking about current feeding practices achieves two goals: it elicits the group's baseline (helping you tailor the session content) and builds engagement by making participants active contributors from the start.

answers.text: Distribute printed pamphlets listing the 8 food groups for participants to study

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Written materials are useful as take-home resources but are not effective openers — many participants in community settings may have limited literacy, and passive reading does not build group engagement.

answers.text: Begin with a pre-test quiz to stratify participants by knowledge level

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A formal quiz can be intimidating and create a hierarchical dynamic. The opening should build trust by acknowledging existing good practices, not by testing knowledge.

overallFeedback.feedback: A community education session should open by asking participants what they currently feed their infants — this elicits baseline knowledge, builds engagement, and acknowledges existing good practices before introducing new content.

Correct! The opening segment should elicit current practices, build engagement, and acknowledge good practices already in place — establishing a participatory tone before moving to the core educational content.
